newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-KULKARNI PILES ON THE AGONY FOR SRI LANKA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-KULKARNI PILES ON THE AGONY FOR SRI LANKA.

text.p: Debutant left-arm spinner Nilesh Kulkarni rounded off an excellent second day for India in the first test against Sri Lanka by taking a wicket with his first delivery.
Earlier, Sachin Tendulkar and Mohammad Azharuddin had become the second and third Indian batsmen after Navjot Sidhu to complete centuries as the touring team amassed 537 for eight declared.
Sri Lanka, left with 11 overs before stumps, lost Marvan Atapattu for 26 in the final over when he drove at Kulkarni's first test delivery and gave wicketkeeper Nayan Mongia a catch.

Kulkarni jointed a group of 11 other bowlers who have performed the feat and only the second Asian after Pakistan leg spinner Intikhab Alam. He took a wicket with his first ball in the 1959-60 series against Australia in Karachi.
Before Kulkarni struck, to leave Sri Lanka on 39 for one, the day was dominated by Tendulkar and Azharuddin.
The overnight pair put on 221 for the fourth wicket, a record for India in tests against Sri Lanka. It beat the previous highest of 163 by Sunil Gavaskar and Azharuddin at Kanpur in 1986-87.
Their stand was finally ended when Tendulkar lofted off-spinner Muthiah Muralitharan to long-on where Mahela Jayawardena took a fine, running catch.
The Indian captain faced 247 balls and hit 20 fours in his 143 -- his third century against Sri Lanka.
Sri Lanka, who had laboured on a lifeless pitch for almost five hours for a wicket, captured another almost immediately when Saurav Ganguly was dismissed without scoring.
The left-hander attempted to cut left-arm spinner Sanath Jayasuriya and was caught at slip by Roshan Mahanama.
Azharuddin's 18th test century put him second in the list of top century-makers for India behind Sunil Gavaskar who hit 34 hundreds.
He fell for 126 to the first ball after tea when he hit a return catch to Muralitharan. Azharuddin batted for 223 minutes, faced 199 balls and hit 11 fours.
